topic.name: Integration Using the Hyperbolic Pythagorean Identities

question.text: Calculate $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle{\int} \left(5 + 2x^2 - 5 anh^2(4x-1) ight ) \, extrm{d}x=$
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity \[ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} 1 + \tan^2 \theta= \sec^2{\theta}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity:

\[ 1-\tanh^2\theta=\sech^2{\theta} \]

Setting $\theta = 4x-1,$ we get

\begin{align} 1-\tanh^2 {(4x-1)} &=\sech^2 {(4x-1)}. \end{align}

Substituting the above into our integral gives \begin{align} \int \left(5 + 2x^2 - 5\tanh^2(4x-1)\right ) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int \bigg(2x^2+5-5\tanh^2 {(4x-1)}\bigg ) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int \bigg(2x^2+5\left[1-\tanh^2 {(4x-1)} \right]\bigg ) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int \bigg(2x^2+5\sech^2 {(4x-1)}\bigg ) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=2\cdot \dfrac{x^3}{3}+5\left(\dfrac{1}{4} \tanh {(4x-1)} \right)+C\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2x^3}{3}+\dfrac{5}{4} \tanh {(4x-1)}+C. \end{align}

example.title: Integrating Hyperbolic Functions With Linear Arguments

question.text: Calculate $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle{\int} 5\coth^2 x \, extrm{d}x=$
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cosecant-cotangent identity \[ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} 1 + \cot^2 x= \csc^2{x}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic cosecant-cotangent identity \[ \coth^2x - 1=\csch^2{x}. \]

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and compute it, as follows: \[\eqalign{ \int 5\coth^2 x \, \textrm{d}x &=\int 5(\csch^2 x +1 )\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\int (5\csch^2 x +5 )\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -5\coth{x}+5x + C }\]

example.title: Integrating a Function Using the Hyperbolic Cosecant-Cotangent Identity

question.text: Calculate $ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle{\int \dfrac{3}{2+2\sinh^2(1-3x)} \, extrm{d}x}=$
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity \[ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \cos^2{\theta} + \sin^2{\theta} = 1. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity \[ \cosh^2{\theta} - \sinh^2{\theta} = 1. \]

Setting $\theta = 1 - 3x,$ we get \begin{align} \cosh^2(1-3x) - \sinh^2(1-3x) & = 1\\[3pt] \cosh^2(1-3x) & = 1 + \sinh^2(1-3x). \end{align}

Using the above, we rewrite and calculate the integral, as follows: \begin{align} \int \dfrac{3}{2+2\sinh^2(1-3x)} \, \textrm{d}x & = \int \dfrac{3}{2\left(1 + \sinh^2(1-3x)\right)} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int \dfrac{3}{2\cosh^2(1-3x)} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{2}\int \dfrac{1}{\cosh^2(1-3x)} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{2} \int \sech^2(1-3x)\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\tanh(1-3x) \right) + C\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{1}{2}\tanh(1-3x) + C \end{align}

example.title: Integrating Hyperbolic Functions With Linear Arguments

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity \[ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} 1 + \tan^2 x= \sec^2{x}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity \[ 1-\tanh^2x=\sech^2{x}. \]

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

\begin{align*} \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \left(\coth^2 x-\coth^2 x \tanh^2 x\right)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \coth^2 x\cdot\left(1- \tanh^2 x\right)\, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \coth^2 x\cdot \sech^2{x}\, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \dfrac{\cosh^2 x}{\sinh^2 x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\cosh^2 x} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \dfrac{1}{\sinh^2{x}} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4} \csch^2{x} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= -\coth x\Big|_{\ln 2}^{\ln 4}\\[5pt] &= -\big(\coth(\ln 4)-\coth(\ln 2)\big)\\[5pt] &= \coth(\ln 2)-\coth(\ln 4)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{\ln 2}+e^{-\ln 2}}{e^{\ln 2}-e^{-\ln 2}}-\dfrac{e^{\ln 4}+e^{-\ln 4}}{e^{\ln 4}-e^{-\ln 4}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2+2^{-1}}{2-2^{-1}}-\dfrac{4+4^{-1}}{4-4^{-1}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{3}-\dfrac{17}{15}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{8}{15}} \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Function Using the Hyperbolic Secant-Tangent Identity

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cotangent-cosecant identity \[ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \csc^2 x -1 = \cot^2 x. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity \[ 1+\csch^2 x=\coth^2 x. \]

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

\begin{align*} \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{1-\csch^4 x}{\csch^2 x\,\coth^2 x - \coth^2 x}\, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{\left(1+\csch^2 x\right)\left(1-\csch^2 x\right)}{-\coth^2 x \left(1-\csch^2 x\right)}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{1+\csch^2 x}{-\coth^2 x}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{\coth^2 x}{-\coth^2 x}\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -\int_{2}^{4} \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -x\Big|_{2}^{4}\\[5pt] &= -\big(4-2\big)\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2} \end{align*}
